lead: Video-game hardware a person owns, organised by platform family: consoles and handhelds (platform → revision → region), game media as objects, controllers, accessories, modding and repair, VR & XR, and arcade and pinball machines; game titles live in the Interactive Entertainment taxonomy.

depts.note: Organised platform → revision (model, slim, special edition) → region; titles are out of scope.

b.v: the system and its library (compatibility, backward compatibility) > performance for the price (resolution, frame rate; Pro against standard model) > disc or digital edition and storage > controller and screen
b.w: Carried over from the previous edition's buying order.

b.v: implementation (original hardware > FPGA > emulation) > video output > screen > build
b.w: Carried over; FPGA vs emulation is the standard collector distinction.

b.v: loose < boxed < complete in box (CIB) < sealed; region (NTSC-J, NTSC-U, PAL)
b.w: Usual collector-market grading, as in price guides such as PriceCharting.

s.brief: Archetype = platform family (Atari 2600, NES/Famicom, Mega Drive/Genesis, SNES, PlayStation 1–5, Saturn, N64, Dreamcast, GameCube, Xbox family, Wii/Wii U, Neo Geo AES, PC Engine/TurboGrafx, 3DO, Jaguar, ColecoVision, Intellivision, Vectrex, Channel F, Odyssey 2, Master System) with revisions as versions (slim, Pro, Series S/X, Model 2, AV Famicom, Wii mini, digital edition) and regional names. Order by generation and significance, not alphabet. Move FPGA, clone and multi-system machines (Analogue, Hyperkin RetroN, Retro-Bit, Polymega, Atari 2600+/7800+, Plaion M64, MiSTer) out of Home console into the FPGA/clone kind. Educational/kids consoles (V.Smile, Sega Pico, Beena) stay as versions under their platform. Use per-generation lists on Wikipedia/Wikidata for sourcing.

k.brief: One archetype per platform family; revisions as versions.
New: FPGA re-implementations (Analogue Super Nt/Mega Sg/3D, MiSTer), clone and multi-system consoles (RetroN, Retro-Bit, Polymega), licensed re-releases taking original carts (Atari 2600+).

s.brief: Archetype = handheld family (Game Boy line, DS/3DS line, PSP, Vita, Game Gear, Lynx, Neo Geo Pocket, WonderSwan, TurboExpress, Switch line, Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Legion Go, Analogue Pocket, Playdate, Evercade) with revisions as versions. Split handheld gaming PCs and Android/Linux emulation handhelds (Anbernic, Miyoo, Retroid, AYN, TrimUI, Powkiddy) into their own kinds; cut the long Anbernic SKU list to series archetypes (RG35XX, RG353, RG40XX, RG Cube) and keep ~5–12 makers.

k.brief: Dedicated handhelds from console makers and boutique (Playdate, Analogue Pocket, Evercade).
Switch family; revisions as versions.
New: x86 PC handhelds (Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Legion Go, MSI Claw, GPD Win, Ayaneo); move these models from Handheld console.
New: Linux/Android retro handhelds (Anbernic, Miyoo, Retroid, AYN Odin/Thor, TrimUI, Powkiddy) and the GP2X/Dingoo lineage; move these models from Handheld console.

s.brief: Built-in-game machines: early dedicated Pong-era consoles (Magnavox Odyssey, Atari Home Pong, Color TV-Game), official mini re-releases (NES/SNES Classic, Mega Drive Mini, PC Engine Mini, PlayStation Classic, Neo Geo mini, Astro City Mini) and licensed plug-and-play lines (Atari Flashback, Jakks TV Games) as archetypes; Game & Watch series as archetypes for LCD handhelds (Silver, Gold, Wide Screen, Multi Screen, New Wide Screen, Panorama…) plus Tiger LCD, Mattel Electronics handhelds; tabletop VFD games (Coleco, Epoch, Grandstand, Tomy, Game & Watch Table Top). Trim repetitive Jakks/AtGames SKUs.

k.brief: Split Pong-era dedicated consoles as an archetype group; minis by maker line.
Game & Watch series as archetypes; Tiger, Mattel Electronics, modern Super Pocket line.
VFD/LCD tabletop games by maker line.

s.brief: Collector add-ons that extend a console: disk/CD drives (Famicom Disk System, Mega-CD, TurboGrafx-CD, 64DD, Jaguar CD), hardware upgrades (32X, Expansion Pak), converters and adapters for other systems or regions (Super Game Boy, Game Boy Player, Power Base Converter, region converters). Name the add-on as archetype with model revisions as versions. Sega Mega-CD appears in both k7 and k9: keep it in Disk-drive add-on only.

depts.note: The game as an object: carrier format, edition, region and completeness; titles live in the Interactive Entertainment taxonomy.

b.v: platform > region > completeness (loose, complete, sealed) > edition (standard, limited, collector's) > grade (WATA, VGA)
b.w: Collector order; grading services from the cross-category Grading-services register.

s.brief: Archetype = carrier format (Atari 2600 cartridge, NES Game Pak, Famicom cassette, SNES/Super Famicom cartridge, Mega Drive cartridge, HuCard, N64 Game Pak, Game Boy Game Pak, GD-ROM, mini-DVD GameCube disc, UMD, Blu-ray game disc, Nintendo Game Card, PS Vita card, Famicom Disk card, cassette tape games for home computers). Versions = regional variants and special editions (black-box NES, gold Zelda cart, limited-run prints). Add edition types (collector's edition, limited print run e.g. Limited Run Games, Greatest Hits/Platinum/Player's Choice reprints) as types, not titles. Never list game titles.

k.brief: New: boxed special edition with extras (art book, statue, steelbook); edition type only, no title list.
New: sealed or loose game encapsulated and graded by a service (WATA, VGA, CGC); cross-link to the Grading-services register.

s.brief: Restraint only: keep as kind-level entries, no models. Give DLC a proper source-less definition; keep Expansion / Add-on pack as types.

depts.note: Tier for mainstream pads; variety for sim, arcade and retro controllers.

b.v: works on your system (licensed for Xbox and PS5) > stick technology (Hall effect or TMR over potentiometer, against drift) > build and ergonomics > latency and polling rate > rear paddles and remapping
b.w: Carried over; RTINGS controller tests use similar axes.

b.v: lever or leverless layout > parts (Sanwa / Seimitsu levers and buttons) > platform support and latency
wheelbase torque and drive type (gear < belt < direct drive) > pedals (potentiometer < load cell < hydraulic) > ecosystem and rim compatibility > rig rigidity

s.brief: Archetype = first-party pad lineage (NES pad, SNES pad, Genesis 3/6-button, PlayStation pad → DualShock → DualSense/Edge, N64, GameCube/WaveBird, Xbox Duke → S → 360 → Wireless/Elite, Switch Pro, Joy-Con) plus key third-party lines (8BitDo, Hori, PowerA, GameSir, Razer, Scuf, Xbox Adaptive). Arcade sticks: Hori RAP, Mad Catz TE, Qanba, Victrix, NES Advantage; leverless: Hit Box (originator), Snack Box, Haute42, Razer Kitsune, Victrix KO. Cut third-party SKU noise to ~8–12 per kind.

Archetypes by maker line: Logitech Driving Force/G29/G923/RS, Thrustmaster T300/T-GT/T818, Fanatec CSL/ClubSport/Podium, Moza R-series, Simucube, Simagic, Asetek; pedals (Heusinkveld, load cell sets); shifters (TH8A, Fanatec SQ); rigs (Playseat, Next Level Racing, Trak Racer, Sim-Lab aluminium profile). Racing wheel = complete wheel-and-pedal sets; wheelbase = rimless motor; add steering rim / button box as a new kind. Move rudder pedals out of Pedal set to Flight controls via brief (keep in this kind as type if simpler).

k.brief: New: interchangeable rim or button box for a wheelbase (formula, GT, round).

s.brief: Archetypes: Thrustmaster HOTAS Cougar → Warthog, T.16000M, T.Flight; Saitek/Logitech X52/X56; VKB Gladiator/Gunfighter; Virpil; Winwing; Honeycomb Alpha/Bravo; Turtle Beach VelocityOne. Add rudder pedals (move from Pedal set) and keep control panels as kind with makers (Logitech/Saitek panels, Winwing MFDs).

k.brief: New: foot pedals for yaw/brakes in flight sims (Thrustmaster TFRP/TPR, Honeycomb Charlie, MFG Crosswind).

s.brief: Retro collector controllers: light-gun lineage (Nintendo Zapper, Light Phaser, Super Scope, Menacer, Justifier, GunCon 1–3, modern Sinden and GUN4IR for flat screens), motion (Power Glove, Wii Remote/MotionPlus, PlayStation Move, Ring-Con), cameras (EyeToy, Kinect), console mice, paddles/spinners (Atari paddle, Arkanoid Vaus).

Archetypes: Guitar Hero (RedOctane SG/X-plorer/Les Paul) and Rock Band (Stratocaster/Telecaster) guitars, Rock Band/Guitar Hero drum kits, DJ Hero and beatmania turntables, Taiko drum, DK Bongos, Samba de Amigo maracas; dance pads (DDR, Power Pad, L-TEK, StepManiaX), Wii Balance Board; SingStar microphones. Rename 'Other rhythm controllers' to a clear kind name.

k.n: Turntable, drum and other rhythm controller
k.brief: Turntables, taiko, bongos, maracas, keyboard controllers.

depts.note: Quality-of-life items: right kind and what makes a good one; accessory SKUs trimmed to market-covering brands.

b.v: made for your exact model > first-party or licensed > build and fit > price

s.brief: Restraint: trim each kind to ~5–8 market-covering brands (Nintendo, Sony, PowerA, Hori, dbrand, Spigen, JSAUX). Move VR cases to the VR accessories shelf by brief only (keep here as models if simpler). Drop 'Nintendo 64 Game Storage Tower' noise or keep as storage type.

Restraint: one AC adapter entry with first-party plus 2–3 aftermarket makers, not one model per console; VR battery straps out of battery packs (VR shelf handles head straps). Trim no-name Amazon cooling stands to a few brands.

Restraint: cut per-console cable SKUs to cable types (RF, composite, S-Video, RGB SCART, component, HDMI, link cable) as `t` types with makers (first-party, Retro Access, Retro Game Cables, Hyperkin). Memory cards: first-party formats only plus Seagate expansion. Multitaps and controller converters kept.

Collector-relevant first-party peripherals: Rumble Pak (originator) and Dreamcast Jump/Vibration Packs, console keyboards (Family BASIC, Dreamcast keyboard, Xbox 360 Chatpad), media remotes and TV tuners, Toys-to-Life portals (Skylanders, Disney Infinity, LEGO Dimensions). Trim third-party rumble clones to a few.

depts.note: Parts and tools owners swap to upgrade, restore or play originals on modern displays.

b.v: RF < composite < S-Video < RGB/component < digital (HDMI mod or scaler); scaler lag and line-multiplication quality

s.brief: Archetypes: flash carts (EverDrive by Krikzz, Mig Flash, SD2SNES/FXPak Pro, EZ-Flash, R4), optical drive emulators (GDEMU, Rhea/Phoebe, XStation, MODE, Terraonion), modchips and soft-mod hardware, IPS/backlight screen kits (Game Boy IPS, FunnyPlaying), replacement shells, reproduction cartridges, HDMI internal mods (UltraHDMI, Retro GEM, Carby), video scalers (OSSC, RetroTINK 2X/4K, Framemeister), cheat devices (Game Genie, Action Replay, GameShark). Repair: one Replacement part entry (Hall-effect/TMR sticks, batteries, fans, screens) and toolkits (iFixit, 8BitDo). Cut iFixit SKU list to part types.

k.brief: New: board replacing a console's disc drive to load games from SD/USB.
New: chip or board that bypasses region or copy protection on a console.
New: external box converting retro video to modern displays (OSSC, RetroTINK, Framemeister).

k.n: Internal HDMI or RGB mod kit
k.brief: New: board installed in a console for digital or RGB output.
New: IPS/backlight replacement screen kit for a handheld.
New: aftermarket housing for a handheld or controller.
New: aftermarket-made cartridge of a game or homebrew; note authenticity concerns.

b.v: display (resolution, panel, lenses) > comfort and weight > tracking (inside-out vs base station) > library and platform > value
b.w: Carried over; matches reviewer test axes.

s.brief: Archetype = headset line (Oculus Rift DK1 → CV1 → Rift S; Quest 1→2→3/3S, Pro; HTC Vive → Pro → Pro 2, Focus; Valve Index; PlayStation VR/VR2; Pimax; Varjo; Bigscreen Beyond; Apple Vision Pro; Samsung Galaxy XR; Pico; Windows Mixed Reality). Enterprise-only units (Varjo XR, ThinkReality, StarVR, VRgineers) drop to kind-level mention per scope rule. Add XR glasses (Xreal, Viture, Rokid) as a new kind.

k.brief: New: glasses that show a virtual screen from a phone, console or PC (Xreal, Viture, Rokid).

s.brief: Kinds owners buy to extend a headset: tracked controllers (Oculus Touch, Valve Index Knuckles, PS VR2 Sense — cross-link Motion controller), trackers and base stations (Vive Tracker, SteamVR Base Station 1.0/2.0), head straps incl. battery straps and facial interfaces (BOBOVR, KIWI Design, Meta Elite Strap), omnidirectional treadmills (Virtuix Omni, KAT Walk), haptic vests and gloves (bHaptics). Keep makers to ~5–10 per kind.

k.n: VR head strap or facial interface

depts.note: Coin-op video cabinets, boards and pinball owned by collectors; home replicas included.

b.v: original dedicated cabinet > conversion > reproduction or home replica; working condition, original artwork and monitor (CRT) status
b.w: Collector convention as in the Killer List of Videogames / Internet Pinball Database.

s.brief: Archetype = cabinet model (Sega Astro City/New Astro City/Blast City/Aero City, Taito Egret/Vewlix, Namco Noir, SNK Neo Geo MVS cabinets; dedicated US uprights by form). Arcade1Up and similar 3/4-scale home replicas move to the new Home replica cabinet kind (bar-top Counter-cades stay in Bar-top). Use the Killer List of Videogames (arcade-museum.com) cabinet categories as the axis. Trim SNK cabinet SKU list to families.

k.brief: Japanese candy cabinets; clarify name and definition.
New: reduced-scale cabinet made for homes (Arcade1Up, iiRcade, AtGames Legends Ultimate).

s.brief: Archetype = system board family (Sega System 16/Model 2/NAOMI, Capcom CPS-1/2/3, Neo Geo MVS, Namco System 22, Taito Type X, Konami System 573, Nintendo VS./PlayChoice-10). Add consumer-owned parts: JAMMA supergun/consolized setups, arcade levers and buttons (Sanwa JLF/OBSF, Seimitsu, Happ), arcade CRT monitors (Wells-Gardner, Nanao), multi-game boards (Pandora's Box) noted as trade/bootleg.

k.brief: New: unit that runs JAMMA boards at home on a TV.
New: replacement joystick levers and pushbuttons (Sanwa, Seimitsu, Happ).
New: CRT or LCD monitor made for arcade cabinets.

s.brief: Archetypes by era and maker: electromechanical pinball (Gottlieb, Williams, Bally 1947–1978), solid-state (Bally, Williams, Gottlieb/Premier, Stern, Data East), modern (Stern, Jersey Jack Pinball, Spooky, Chicago Gaming remakes, American Pinball); Williams/Bally WPC era icons as archetypes (e.g. Addams Family, Twilight Zone — machine models, which are physical products, not entertainment titles). Digital/virtual pinball cabinets (Arcade1Up, AtGames Legends Pinball, VPin builds). Electromechanical arcade games (Sega Periscope, gun and driving EMs). Source from the Internet Pinball Database (ipdb.org) and Pinside.

k.brief: New: aftermarket toppers, lighting kits and playfield mods.
